name: Newfoundland and Labrador: public health coverage for newcomers
name_fr: Terre-Neuve-et-Labrador : assurance maladie publique pour les nouveaux arrivants
description: Who is covered by Medical Care Plan (MCP) by immigration status, any waiting period for newcomers, how to apply, the public drug-coverage model and the share of adults with a regular health care provider.

attributes.legal_status: in force (eligibility rules as published on the access date)

eligibility_by_status.citizen: Eligible as a resident (residency and presence rules apply).
eligibility_by_status.permanent_resident: Eligible; first coverage is valid for one year, then renewable for up to five years; interim coverage possible while a PR card is pending.
eligibility_by_status.work_permit_holder: Eligible with a permit valid at least 12 months plus an employer letter confirming 12 months' full-time work (6 months for NLPNP and Atlantic Immigration Program participants); coverage up to one year at a time.
eligibility_by_status.study_permit_holder: Eligible with a study permit valid at least 12 months for full-time enrolment; renew annually.
eligibility_by_status.visitor: Not eligible (visitors and tourists are excluded from every provincial plan reviewed).

attributes.status_dependency: Which rule applies depends on the user's immigration status, which is unknown (USER-PROFILE.md: 'Citizenship(s) and current country of residence', 'Existing Canadian status or application').

newcomer_waiting_period.arriving_from_outside_canada: No fixed wait: coverage starts on the latest of arrival in NL, start of full-time employment (workers) or approval.
newcomer_waiting_period.moving_from_another_province: People relocating keep their previous plan for the rest of the arrival month plus two months (MCP form, via search extract).

attributes.how_to_apply: Application form with copies of documents, by mail, fax, email or drop-off; typical response two weeks.
attributes.drug_coverage_model: Newfoundland and Labrador Prescription Drug Program: Access, Assurance (income-based deductible) and 65Plus plans (PMPRB 2020/21 summary).

regular_provider.source: CIHI indicator 'Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider', Statistics Canada CCHS

sources.title: Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider — indicator data table (data updated October 2026); underlying data: Statistics Canada, Canadian Community Health Survey, Annual Component
sources.methodology: Weighted percent of adults 18+ reporting a regular/primary health care provider (family doctor, nurse practitioner or other); 95% confidence interval given. 2025 adult questions were harmonized, so compare with earlier years with caution.

sources.title: Public Drug Plan Designs, 2021/22 edition (describes 2020/21 plan designs; page modified 2024-01-30)

verification.notes: Provincial page(s) fetched directly where status is 'verified'; otherwise some content came from search-engine extracts of official pages (403 or bot-check on fetch). Regular-provider figures parsed from CIHI's published data table.

limitations: Eligibility text summarises official pages and is not legal advice; temporary-status rules change often. Drug-plan designs are from PMPRB's 2020/21 summary and may be out of date. 'Without a regular provider' is 100 minus the CIHI share (simple arithmetic).
